targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands delegated agents, approval gates and conversation roles.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A downstream agent can receive prose claiming that a user approved an action, but the wording alone cannot establish who actually supplied the authorization.

whyNow: A same-day merged Codex change carries bounded, role-preserving root-conversation evidence into MultiAgent V2 Guardian review while excluding synthetic and forwarded authorization claims.

externalHook.description: The same sentence can be authorization evidence or untrusted context depending on its structured origin and role.

coreProposition: For delegated digital employees, authorization provenance should travel through a structured review-plane evidence channel whose authoritative source and role remain separate from work-plane prose; this improves admission decisions, but long-lived, scoped and revocable authority still requires a distinct durable authorization state.

originalValue.description: Separates role-preserving evidence used at a review point from the durable authorization state required to carry principal, scope, freshness and revocation across time.

readerTakeaway: Treat agent-forwarded approval claims as context, bind review evidence to an authoritative source and structured role, and represent persistent authority with an independently governed state machine.

supported: Merged Codex code resolves the actual root thread and preserves User and Assistant roles for bounded Guardian review evidence.
Only structured root-user messages are designated as authorization evidence; assistant and forwarded claims remain context.
Synthetic summaries, user_action items and review artifacts are excluded from the root authorization feed.
The evidence channel is bounded and isolated from the ordinary worker model context.
unsupported: Cryptographic authentication of the human principal
A durable authorization ledger or reusable capability token
Coverage of every approval path or arbitrary subagent operation
uncertain: How approvals and revocations should persist after the evidence window rotates
Which review paths need capability-style authorization rather than conversational evidence

firstPartyRole.rationale: The article develops a general authorization-provenance pattern for delegated agent systems without relying on a first-party project.

decisionReason: The merged implementation supplies a concrete boundary, and the Research Object adds a transferable model that distinguishes review evidence from durable authorization state.
